notes: What the app gets wrong today. Each entry prints as KNOWN on every run and does not fail it. An entry that stops matching fails the run until it is taken off the list, so a fix is always noticed. The contrast entries are one per screen, theme and color pair, each with the ratio the app draws. The language entries are one per kind of word the API cannot send in Spanish yet, which stay until it does, and one per place the portal itself still draws English, which the build that fixes it takes off. A too small entry names the control and why it is under 44 today.

accepted.why: The person's name in the header runs to one line and ends in an ellipsis when there is no room. Accepted: the name is theirs to recognise at a glance, the avatar beside it is the way to their profile, and the whole name is on the Profile screen.
The role under the name runs to one line and ends in an ellipsis the same way, and for the same reason.

An unfinished report's title on Help runs to one line and ends in an ellipsis when there is no room, the way a name does. The stub serves the first form's title in Spanish from this build on, and the Spanish is longer.
The role under the name, in Spanish now, runs to one line and ends in an ellipsis the same way the English one does, and for the same reason.
An admin's role under the name runs to one line and ends in an ellipsis the same way a custodian's does, and for the same reason.
An admin's role in Spanish, the same way, and for the same reason.

failures.what: is a to-do item the API sent in English
failures.why: A to-do item and its instructions are written in English in the database and the API sends them as written. The API's build gives them Spanish and sends the language the request asks for.

failures.what: is a to-do zone the API sent in English
failures.why: A to-do item's zone is written in English in the database and sent as written, the same as the item.

failures.what: is a supply the API sent in English
failures.why: A supply's name and its unit are written in English in the database and sent as written.

failures.what: is a notice the API sent in English
failures.why: An in-app notice is written by the API in English at the moment it is sent. The API's build writes it in the person's saved language.

failures.what: is an inspection item the API sent in English
failures.why: An inspection's name, its items and their zones are written in English in the database and sent as written.

failures.what: is a service the API sent in English
failures.why: A shift's service is written in English in the database and sent as written.

failures.what: is a site role the API sent in English
failures.why: A person's role at a site is typed by an admin, in English today, and sent as typed.

failures.what: is a shift name the API sent in English
failures.why: A shift's name is typed by an admin, in English today, and sent as typed.

failures.what: is a Help reply the API sent in English
failures.why: Help's replies, the fixed ones included, arrive from the API in English. The route already carries the language; the reply's language is the API's to change.

failures.what: is a procedure name the API sent in English
failures.why: The procedures an answer cites are named the way the API writes them, in English. Their names are the API's to send in the person's language, with Help's replies. The suite draws one for the first time in this build.
